title: Constrain a frontend and its identity
instructions:
All commands and files belong on the initial controller. Use the supplied kubeconfig and `sudo` for root-owned paths. This exam has one node, no workers, and no context switching.

Pod `frontend` in `helix` exposes `/usr/share/nginx/html/staff/`. Load the supplied AppArmor profile `/etc/apparmor.d/site-guard` and recreate the Pod using it so the private directory cannot be read. Keep the public site serving HTTP. Inspect the existing service accounts and select the non-default account with the least privileges. Delete the other unused non-default service accounts; do not create accounts or use `default`. Preserve the existing image and content volume. You can test locally with `kubectl -n helix exec frontend -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1/staff/`.
steps: Compare RoleBindings and Role rules for the existing accounts.
Load the profile on the only node.
Recreate the Pod with the Localhost profile and selected account; remove unused accounts.
Verify public HTTP succeeds and private-file reads fail.

title: Repair selected CIS failures
instructions: Use installed `kube-bench` with `--config-dir /opt/kube-bench/cfg --benchmark cis-1.10`. Repair only these seeded FAILs: kubelet service unit permissions (`/usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service`, 4.1.1), kubelet configuration permissions (`/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`, 4.1.9), etcd data-directory ownership (`/var/lib/etcd`, 1.1.12), and profiling for kube-controller-manager (1.3.2) and kube-scheduler (1.4.1). Use the benchmark's recommended values; create system user/group `etcd` if needed. Other benchmark findings, including API-server and policy findings, are out of scope. Keep the API server and control-plane components healthy.
steps: Run kube-bench with the specified benchmark and inspect only the five requested checks.
Apply restrictive file modes and the etcd ownership.
Set --profiling=false in the two static Pod manifests.
Wait for the components to restart and rerun the selected checks.
solution:
sudo python3 - <<'PY'
import yaml
from pathlib import Path
import os, pwd, grp, subprocess
for p in ['/usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service','/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml']:
    os.chmod(p, 0o600)
subprocess.run(['groupadd','--system','etcd'], check=False)
subprocess.run(['useradd','--system','--gid','etcd','--no-create-home','etcd'], check=False)
os.chown('/var/lib/etcd', pwd.getpwnam('etcd').pw_uid, grp.getgrnam('etcd').gr_gid)
for name in ['kube-controller-manager','kube-scheduler']:
    p=Path('/etc/kubernetes/manifests')/(name+'.yaml')
    obj=yaml.safe_load(p.read_text())
    cmd=obj['spec']['containers'][0]['command']
    cmd[:]=[a for a in cmd if not a.startswith('--profiling=')]+['--profiling=false']
    tmp=p.with_name('.'+p.name+'.tmp')
    text=yaml.safe_dump(obj)
    if text!=p.read_text():
        tmp.write_text(text); tmp.replace(p)

title: Customize runtime threat alerts
instructions:
A Pod using `httpd:2.4-alpine` in `runtime-watch` repeatedly writes below a binary directory. Falco reports alerts beginning `File below a known binary directory opened for writing`. Identify the responsible rule and override it using `/etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml`, not the default rules file. Set priority `CRITICAL` and output exactly:

`File below a known binary directory opened for writing (user_id=%user.uid file_updated=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline)`

Configure Falco to write text alerts to `/opt/runtime-incidents/events.log`, then restart service `falco`. Keep monitoring and the suspicious workload running. New alerts may take up to 30 seconds.
steps: Search the default rules for the alert message and identify Write below binary dir.
Use the override replace syntax for output and priority in the local rules file.
Enable file output, restart Falco, and inspect newly emitted alerts.
solution:
sudo python3 - <<'PY'
import yaml
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('/etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml')
p.write_text(yaml.safe_dump([{'rule':'Write below binary dir','priority':'CRITICAL',
    'output':'File below a known binary directory opened for writing (user_id=%user.uid file_updated=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline)', 'override':{'priority':'replace','output':'replace'}}]))
p=Path('/etc/falco/falco.yaml')
obj=yaml.safe_load(p.read_text())
obj['file_output']={'enabled':True,'keep_alive':False,'filename':'/opt/runtime-incidents/events.log'}
p.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(obj))
Path('/opt/runtime-incidents').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
PY
sudo systemctl restart falco
for i in $(seq 1 30); do sudo grep -q 'Critical File below a known binary directory' /opt/runtime-incidents/events.log 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 1; done

title: Enable and scope API audit logging
instructions: Enable API-server auditing using `/etc/kubernetes/security-policy.yaml`. Write logs to `/var/log/security-audit.log`, with retention 7 days, maximum size 12 MB, and maximum 4 backup files. Update the supplied policy to record secret deletions (including collection deletion) in `kube-system` at Metadata level; Deployment changes (create/update/patch/delete/deletecollection) in `default` at Request level; and every other request at Metadata level. Ensure the running API server uses the policy and keep it healthy. A recovery manifest is at `/root/backup/kube-apiserver.yaml`: restore it to `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml` if necessary. Q14 and Q15 both edit this manifest; preserve each other's settings.
steps: Edit the policy with specific rules before the catch-all.
Add API-server flags and hostPath mounts for policy and logs.
Wait for API recovery; inspect real events for each scope.
solution:
sudo python3 - <<'PY'
import yaml
from pathlib import Path
policy={'apiVersion': 'audit.k8s.io/v1', 'kind': 'Policy', 'rules': [{'level': 'Metadata', 'verbs': ['delete', 'deletecollection'], 'namespaces': ['kube-system'], 'resources': [{'group': '', 'resources': ['secrets']}]}, {'level': 'Request', 'verbs': ['create', 'update', 'patch', 'delete', 'deletecollection'], 'namespaces': ['default'], 'resources': [{'group': 'apps', 'resources': ['deployments']}]}, {'level': 'Metadata'}]}
Path('/etc/kubernetes/security-policy.yaml').write_text(yaml.safe_dump(policy))
p=Path('/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml')
obj=yaml.safe_load(p.read_text())
c=obj['spec']['containers'][0]
values={'audit-policy-file':'/etc/kubernetes/security-policy.yaml','audit-log-path':'/var/log/security-audit.log',
        'audit-log-maxage':'7','audit-log-maxsize':'12','audit-log-maxbackup':'4'}
c['command']=[a for a in c['command'] if not any(a.startswith('--'+key+'=') for key in values)]
c['command'] += ['--'+key+'='+value for key,value in values.items()]
for name,host,mount,ro,typ in [('audit-policy','/etc/kubernetes/security-policy.yaml','/etc/kubernetes/security-policy.yaml',True,'File'),
                              ('audit-log','/var/log','/var/log',False,'Directory')]:
    obj['spec']['volumes']=[v for v in obj['spec']['volumes'] if v['name']!=name]
    obj['spec']['volumes'].append({'name':name,'hostPath':{'path':host,'type':typ}})
    c['volumeMounts']=[v for v in c['volumeMounts'] if v['name']!=name]
    c['volumeMounts'].append({'name':name,'mountPath':mount,'readOnly':ro})
tmp=p.with_name('.'+p.name+'.tmp'); text=yaml.safe_dump(obj)
if text!=p.read_text():
    tmp.write_text(text); tmp.replace(p)

title: Integrate fail-closed image admission
instructions: A TLS ImageReview server is already available through Service `image-gate` in `cks001-system`. Integrate it using the API server's **ImagePolicyWebhook** admission plugin (not a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration). Create `/root/CKS/ImageGate/admission-configuration.yaml`. That directory is already mounted in the API server at `/etc/admission-controllers`; reference the supplied kubeconfig there as `/etc/admission-controllers/admission-kubeconfig.yaml`. Reject `latest` images from any repository and fail closed if the webhook is unavailable; do not permit cached approvals to bypass this requirement. Enable the admission controller, preserving existing admission and audit settings. Delete `harbor/harbor-web` and recreate it with the same nginx repository and tag `1.28`, leaving it running. Recovery backup: `/root/backup/kube-apiserver.yaml`; restore it if the API becomes unavailable.
